svg.text: The Ghost Turnip: A Lantern Before Pumpkins
a Samhain plate — ghost turnip, Stingy Jack, the thin veil, root lanterns, the crossing, and the moot · seed 20261023
A · The Ghost Turnip
plaster cast, Donegal, c. 1900 — the original rotted,
as turnips do; the cast is the lantern’s ghost
A · Donated 1943 by a Fintown schoolteacher
who remembered when everyone made them.
B · Stingy Jack’s Two Tricks
trick two: the cross in the bark
trick one: the Devil as a coin,
pocketed beside a silver cross
barred from both doors, he walks
with a coal in a carved-out turnip
B · “Jack of the Lantern” — the name is
a wandering man first, a vegetable second.
C · Samhain: The Veil Thins
the living
the returning dead
sundown Oct 31 → Nov 1: summer’s end, the Celtic new year
C · Before it was Halloween, it was the hinge
of the year — and the door stood ajar.
D · The Whole Root Cellar Applied
turnip
Ireland & Scotland
potato
in some districts
large beet
England
radish
also recorded
metal lanterns were dear; roots were in the ground
D · Faces cut so the light gets out
without the ember dying — a vent and a warning.
E · The Crossing
from Ireland
to America
immigrants carried the custom; the new country
offered a bigger, softer, native canvas
E · Same lantern, new vegetable —
the pumpkin is an American development.
F · The Moot Endures
“moot” — Isle of Man
Hop tu Naa, still sung house to house
the pumpkin — everywhere else
grinning on a million porches
one tradition, two lanterns, both still lit
F · Carve the big soft one for joy —
carve a turnip once, for the shiver.
Plate XIX · The Ghost Turnip — Lapis, atelier, October 23, 2026
